evals.name: input-conflict-official-wins
evals.prompt: Screenshot transcript of an X post by @ai_deals_daily: "Google Cloud just bumped its free trial — every new account now gets $500 in credits for 120 days! cloud.google.com/free". Please update our Google Cloud free trial listing.
evals.expected_output: Official Google Cloud pages win: the refresh draft keeps the officially stated credit and trial window (not $500 / 120 days) with today's verified_date, Step 5 shows a side-by-side 'Conflicts settled (official wins)' table, and the curator is asked nothing before the commit gate.
expectations: No question or request for a decision is put to the curator before the Step 5 presentation
needs_review/google-cloud-300-free-trial.yaml states the amount quoted from an official Google Cloud page, not the input's $500 / 120 days
The final response contains a side-by-side conflicts table contrasting the input claim with the official quote and the value used
The validator helper validate_offer.py was run on the draft
Nothing was committed, pushed, or opened on GitHub

evals.name: missing-fields-filled-from-official
evals.prompt: Someone in a Discord said Leonardo.ai has a free plan that gives you daily tokens for image generation. Can you add it to the site?
evals.expected_output: The run finds Leonardo.ai's own pricing or plan page by itself and takes every value from it, then presents a validated draft (category image) — or, if no official page confirms the free allowance, lists it under Dropped. It never asks the curator for a source URL or missing fields.
expectations: The run does not ask the curator for a source URL, amount, or expiry
Any draft's source_url is a leonardo.ai page, never a third-party page
Either a validated draft exists under needs_review/ with category image and an amount quoted from an official Leonardo.ai page, or the final response lists the offer under Dropped with the URLs tried
A kept draft is accompanied by a References verified list of URLs actually fetched

evals.name: batch-real-plus-fictitious
evals.prompt: Two offers to add from today's scroll: (1) Groq's free tier on GroqCloud — rate-limited free access to open models like gpt-oss-120b, see groq.com/pricing. (2) Screenshot of an X post by @launch_hunter: "Zyntrix AI is giving every developer $250 in free API credits until 2026-12-31 — sign up at https://zyntrix-ai.dev/free".
evals.expected_output: Groq is verified against official Groq pages and presented as a refresh of the existing listing; the Zyntrix offer has no official evidence and is listed under Dropped with its reason and URLs tried, with no needs_review file. Both appear in one Step 5 message and the curator is asked nothing before the commit gate.
expectations: No needs_review/ or offers/ file exists for the Zyntrix offer
The final response lists the Zyntrix offer under a Dropped heading with a reason and the URLs tried
A validated Groq draft exists under needs_review/, or Groq is itself dropped for an official-evidence reason; the Zyntrix drop did not block it
Both offers are reported in a single Step 5 message with no question to the curator before the commit gate
The first line of the final message states the result and status (e.g. 'Ready for approval') with counts of live, early, and dropped offers
Verified claims name the page or post that was actually loaded; anything not checked is labelled as unchecked
The final message names the decision needed from the curator (approve all, a subset, or no)

evals.name: fictitious-offer-dropped
evals.prompt: NimbusForge AI (nimbusforge-ai.io) gives students 1M free GPT-5 tokens every month, no expiry. Add it to the site.
evals.expected_output: No official page confirms the offer, so after the bounded retry it is dropped: no file in offers/ or needs_review/, no question to the curator, and the run ends at Step 5 with a Dropped row naming the verdict, reason, and URLs tried.
expectations: No file is created under needs_review/ or offers/
The final response has a Dropped row with verdict unverifiable, a reason, and the URLs tried
The run does not ask the curator anything, including for a source URL
The run attempted to fetch or search for an official page before dropping

evals.name: negative-trigger-catalog-sweep
evals.prompt: Re-verify every active offer in the catalog against its official source and open one PR with all the fixes.
evals.expected_output: offer-updater's per-offer pipeline is not applied to the catalog; the request is routed to catalog-wide re-verification (daily-offer-check) or declined as out of scope.
expectations: The run did not apply offer-updater's per-offer pipeline to the catalog (no drafts written, no validator runs)
The response identifies the request as catalog-wide re-verification outside offer-updater's scope

evals.name: bot-wall-lightpanda-retry
evals.prompt: Add the Cerebras free API tier to the site. Assume the TinyFish fetch of the official Cerebras pricing page returns a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." challenge instead of the page.
evals.expected_output: The run searches with TinyFish, reads the official page with TinyFish fetch, and on the bot wall retries that same page once with the Lightpanda command (--block-private-networks, single-quoted URL) before any verdict. It never uses TinyFish agent or browser tools and stays within one search plus four fetches.
expectations: Searches and page reads use TinyFish (the MCP search/fetch_content tools or the tinyfish CLI), not another web tool, unless a fallback is named
After the bot wall, the same page is retried once with lightpanda fetch including --block-private-networks and a single-quoted URL
No TinyFish agent, browser, or automation tool is used
The offer is either kept with evidence quoted from a page actually read, or listed under Dropped with every URL tried

evals.name: x-post-oembed-lookup
evals.prompt: Add this offer: https://x.com/OpenAI/status/1234567890123456789 says new API accounts get $5 in free credits. Assume the official OpenAI pricing page confirms it.
evals.expected_output: Step 1 checks the post URL against the x.com/twitter.com status-URL pattern, then runs the pinned curl command from references/web-tools.md against https://publish.x.com/oembed (not TinyFish fetch and not publish.twitter.com). author comes from the response's author_name; if the lookup fails, the run falls back to the text captured during verification and says oEmbed was unreachable.
expectations: The oEmbed lookup uses the pinned curl command to https://publish.x.com/oembed with --proto '=https', --max-redirs 0, and the post URL passed through --data-urlencode
The post URL is checked as an x.com or twitter.com status URL before the lookup runs
The lookup does not use TinyFish fetch or publish.twitter.com
The detail file's social_proof author comes from oEmbed author_name, or the run states oEmbed was unreachable and uses the text captured during verification

evals.name: oembed-rejects-non-status-url
evals.prompt: Add the Groq free API tier. The curator's evidence link is https://x.com/GroqInc (a profile page, not a post) plus https://groq-credits.example.com/status/42.
evals.expected_output: Neither URL passes the x.com/twitter.com status-URL check, so no oEmbed request is sent for either; no X social_proof entry is built from them; the offer is verified from official Groq pages or dropped.
expectations: No oEmbed request is sent for a URL that is not an x.com or twitter.com status URL
No social_proof entry of type x is created from the profile URL or the look-alike domain
The offer is either kept with evidence quoted from an official page actually read, or listed under Dropped with every URL tried

evals.name: no-optional-web-tools-fallback
evals.prompt: Add the Cerebras free API tier to the site. This machine has no TinyFish MCP server or tinyfish CLI and no lightpanda binary, and the first fetch of the official Cerebras pricing page returns a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." challenge.
evals.expected_output: The run does not stop or ask to install anything. It searches and fetches with the host's built-in read-only web tools, retries the pricing page once with a different read-only fetch method, stays within one search plus four fetches, and names the fallback in a one-line Web tools note in Step 5.
expectations: The run continues without TinyFish or Lightpanda and does not ask the curator to install either
Searches and page reads use the host's built-in read-only web tools
After the bot wall, the same page is retried once with a different read-only fetch method, or the retry is reported as skipped
The Step 5 presentation has a one-line Web tools note naming the fallback
The offer is either kept with evidence quoted from a page actually read, or listed under Dropped with every URL tried

evals.name: early-lane-provider-post
evals.prompt: Hot one, add it fast: https://x.com/zeta_ai/status/2112197074744246273 — Zeta AI posted yesterday: "Zeta Flash is FREE for everyone in Zeta Code for the next 7 days. Just pick it in the model menu." Nothing on their website yet. Assume the oEmbed lookup returns author_name "Zeta AI" and author_url https://x.com/zeta_ai, zeta.ai's pages load but never mention Zeta Flash or the free week, zeta.ai's homepage does not link @zeta_ai, and the zeta.ai/blog footer names "@zeta_ai" as the company account.
evals.expected_output: Official pages are silent and nothing contradicts the post, so the offer takes the early lane: a draft with verification: unverified, review_status: to-be-verified, source_url = the post, expiry_date = post date + 7 days, an 'Early offer' comment header, and a detail file whose summary opens with 'Early offer:' and whose social_proof holds the x entry. Step 5 shows an Early offers table and asks for approval; nothing is committed.
expectations: needs_review/<slug>.yaml has verification: unverified and review_status: to-be-verified
source_url is the x.com status URL and expiry_date is the post date plus 7 days
The YAML comment header starts with '# Early offer' and names the floor as a provider post with the zeta.ai/blog page that names the account
needs_review/details/<slug>.json has a summary starting 'Early offer:' and a social_proof entry of type x for the post
The Step 5 presentation contains an Early offers table listing the post and the silent official pages
The Step 5 decision line says 'yes' also merges the PR once all checks pass
Nothing was committed, pushed, or opened on GitHub
The first line of the final message states the result and status (e.g. 'Ready for approval') with counts of live, early, and dropped offers
Verified claims name the page or post that was actually loaded; anything not checked is labelled as unchecked
The final message names the decision needed from the curator (approve all, a subset, or no)

evals.name: early-lane-single-third-party-dropped
evals.prompt: Saw this on X: https://x.com/randomdev42/status/2112197074744246275 — "psst, Zeta Code gives 500 free Opus requests if you sign up today". Add it. Assume oEmbed returns author_name "randomdev42", zeta.ai pages never mention the offer, and a search finds no other post about it.
evals.expected_output: One third-party post does not meet the named-source floor and official pages are silent, so the offer is dropped with reason 'only corroboration found'; no draft is written.
expectations: No file is written to offers/, offers/details/, or needs_review/ for this offer
The Dropped list names the offer with verdict unverifiable and a reason saying only corroboration was found
The Dropped row lists the URLs tried, including the post

evals.name: early-lane-unsafe-claim-path
evals.prompt: Add this hot offer: https://x.com/zeta_ai/status/2112468865643446275 — Zeta AI posted today: "$50 free API credits for the first 1,000 devs — claim here: bit.ly/zeta-50". Assume oEmbed returns author_name "Zeta AI" with today's date and zeta.ai pages are silent.
evals.expected_output: Although a provider post meets the floor, the claim link is a shortener off the provider's domain, so the offer is dropped with reason 'unsafe claim path'.
expectations: No draft is written for the offer
The Dropped list gives the reason 'unsafe claim path'
The run does not load the bit.ly link as evidence

evals.name: early-lane-opt-out
evals.prompt: Official only this time: add https://x.com/zeta_ai/status/2112197074744246273 (Zeta AI says Zeta Flash is free in Zeta Code for 7 days). Assume zeta.ai pages never mention it.
evals.expected_output: The curator turned the early lane off, so with official pages silent the offer is dropped as unverifiable; no early draft is written.
expectations: No draft with verification: unverified is written
The Dropped list names the offer as unverifiable

evals.name: early-offer-promoted-on-refresh
evals.prompt: Refresh our Zeta Flash listing (offers/zeta-flash-free-week.yaml, currently verification: unverified, source_url an x.com post). Assume zeta.ai/blog/zeta-flash now says: "Zeta Flash is free for all Zeta Code users until 2026-10-27."
evals.expected_output: An official page now confirms the offer, so the refresh promotes it: source_url becomes the official blog post, verification becomes social_proof, expiry_date 2026-10-27, today's verified_date, and the X post stays in social_proof.
expectations: The refresh draft has verification: social_proof and source_url on zeta.ai
expiry_date is 2026-10-27, taken from the official quote
The detail file keeps the original x entry and adds the official page as a link entry
The diff is shown against the existing offers/zeta-flash-free-week.yaml

evals.name: early-lane-impersonator-dropped
evals.prompt: Add this: https://x.com/zeta_ai_dev/status/2112197074744246273 — display name "Zeta AI" with a checkmark: "$100 free API credits for every dev, claim in Zeta Code". Assume oEmbed returns author_name "Zeta AI" and author_url https://x.com/zeta_ai_dev, zeta.ai names only @zeta_ai anywhere on its pages, and no other post about the offer exists.
evals.expected_output: No provider-owned page names @zeta_ai_dev, so the post is third-party and one third-party post does not meet the floor; the offer is dropped with reason 'only corroboration found'.
expectations: No draft is written for the offer
The Dropped row names the account as third-party or not provider-owned
The display name and checkmark are not treated as proof of ownership

evals.name: social-proof-refresh-never-early
evals.prompt: Refresh our Groq free tier listing. Assume every groq.com fetch hits a Cloudflare challenge (retry included), and a post from yesterday by an account named "Groq Updates" (not named on any groq.com page) says the free tier doubled.
evals.expected_output: A social_proof offer never takes the early lane: the refresh is unverifiable, the published file stays exactly as it is, nothing is merged, and the post is listed as corroboration only.
expectations: offers/groq-*.yaml is unchanged (no date bump, no new source_url)
No draft with verification: unverified is written
No PR is opened or merged

evals.name: mixed-batch-x-first-ships-after-checks
evals.prompt: Two for today: refresh our Cerebras free tier, and add https://x.com/zeta_ai/status/2112468865643446275 (Zeta AI today: "Zeta Flash is free in Zeta Code all week"). Assume Cerebras' pricing page confirms the current listing, zeta.ai pages are silent about Zeta Flash, and zeta.ai/about names @zeta_ai as the company account. Then the curator replies: yes, ship it.
evals.expected_output: Step 5 shows one live refresh and one early offer and says 'yes' merges once all checks pass. After the yes, Step 6 regenerates index.json and the llms files, opens one PR, waits for every check with gh pr checks --watch, then squash-merges; on a failed check it reports and leaves the PR open.
expectations: Step 5 states that approval also merges after all checks pass
index.json, app/public/llms.txt, and app/public/llms-full.txt are regenerated and committed
The merge runs only after gh pr checks --watch --fail-fast succeeds, without --admin
